body: Forward test of the flags-judgment context method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.55 (naive base rate 0.65) that: Monolithic Power Systems' FY2026 10-K concludes internal control over financial reporting is effective (the deferred-tax material weakness is remediated). Evidence: Q3 2026 10-Q: a material weakness 'related to the accounting for deferred income taxes' associated with 'a one-time tax incentive granted by a certain foreign jurisdiction' was identified at FY2025 year-end; it 'was not remediated as of September 30, 2026'; disclosure controls 'not effective'; management still concluded the financial statements are fairly presented. Business is strong: Q3 2026 revenue $1,202.4m (+63.1% YoY, +22.6% QoQ), non-GAAP gross margin 55.7%, Q4 guide $1,315–1,385m; capacity $6bn → $8bn by H2 2027. Reasoning: Flags-judgment: this flag is narrow (one tax-accounting area, not revenue) and low-teeth for the business, but the event is about remediation itself. Nine months in with no remediation claim and a fast-growing, more complex foreign-tax footprint argues for some slippage; still, single-area tax weaknesses at well-funded companies are usually closed within a year. Resolution: YES if MPWR's 10-K for fiscal year ended 31-Dec-2026 states that internal control over financial reporting was effective as of 31-Dec-2026 and that the previously reported material weakness has been remediated (and no new material weakness is reported). NO otherwise, including if the 10-K is not filed by 15-Mar-2027. Source: SEC EDGAR — MPWR FY2026 Form 10-K, Item 9A. Resolve by 2027-03-15; score with Brier vs base rate.

data.base_rate_reasoning: Reference class (unverified, Audit Analytics-type studies from memory): roughly two-thirds of material weaknesses disclosed in a 10-K are reported remediated in the next annual report.

NO otherwise, including if the 10-K is not filed by 15-Mar-2027.

title: Paper call: Monolithic Power Systems' FY2026 10-K concludes internal control over financial reporting is effective (the deferred-tax material weakness is remediated)
